# Tugra

> Provenance-aware memory for AI agents. Every claim carries its source,
> its age, and its boundary. There is no cloud.

## What it does

- A fact that cannot name where it came from is not a fact.
- Each claim is a file whose frontmatter holds source, last verification date, shelf life, and — when the topic is off-limits — a boundary that forbids invention.
- Search ranks by token score, then freshness, then confidence.
- Retired and rotten facts stay out of the default set.
- Tools: `fact_search`, `fact_read`, `fact_propose`, `event_report`.
- Install: `npx tugra init` creates a vault, writes a sample fact, and prints a config block.
- On a TTY, `npx tugra` prints help and exits. Piped, it is the MCP server.
- License: Apache-2.0. Source: https://github.com/dogrucanemek-alt/tugra

## How to verify

- The three questions asked about agent memory: keeping every claim sourced and verifiable,
  which MCP memory server tracks source/freshness/shelf life, and how a boundary record stops
  invention on a topic with no evidence. Uses the on-disk frontmatter field names:
  https://tugra-ai.com/memory-provenance-for-agents
- Home: https://tugra-ai.com
- Source and format: https://github.com/dogrucanemek-alt/tugra
- The published package name is `tugra`. On a TTY, `npx tugra` prints help.

## Scope — what this deliberately does not claim

- No cloud sync. The vault is the files you pointed at. Nothing is uploaded. (README.md)
- No automatic merge. Two writers, two files. You reconcile. (README.md)
- No delete in this release. Retirement exists; erasure is later. (README.md)
- No automatic conflict detection. Contradictory facts can sit side by side until a human says otherwise. (README.md)
- No hosted service. `npx tugra` is a local stdio process. (README.md)
- This package is not published as a SaaS. There is no price table here. (README.md)
